summary:
SL-008 holds against everything I could reach. The one thing I could not reach is the UAC press itself, which only a person can do.

**What I ran, all from this unelevated shell:**
- **Full suite:** 1643 passed, 0 failed.
- **Fitness:** all 120 rules hold.
- **The slice's exe-level script, on a freshly published exe:** ALL CHECKS HELD.
  - Start-up: no-path and path-window stayed up with no 740.
  - No offer: a folder, a folder with a trailing backslash, and root-unreadable all report the key present and false.
  - The offer: a whole-D: report finished with 2 folders unread and offered=true, read from a visible, in-view button. The pickers' line kept its height.

**My own checks on this PC's real drives:**
- **The product's own probe**, loaded from a fresh App.dll build:
  - C: and D: give Fixed and would offer.
  - E: and F: are removable and not ready, so they give null.
  - Mapped Z: gives Network and is refused.
  - A SUBST letter R: I made gives null.
- **The SUBST letter in report mode:** R:\ finished with 1 folder unread and offered=false.
- **The shipped exe's manifests** all say asInvoker. Nothing in them says requireAdministrator or highestAvailable.
- **Call sites:** the only call to RescanAsAdministrator.Start in src is OnRescanAsAdministrator. No `<Using>` item exists in any project or build file.

**In Windows Sandbox, on the published exe:**
- **Already elevated:** as SYSTEM (elevated), a global SUBST letter that finished with 1 folder unread gave offered=false.
- **Standard user:** a Medium-integrity account through a task, on the same setup, gave offered=true.
- **Fully read drive:** the same account on a clean global letter finished with 0 unread and gave offered=false.
- **UNC share roots:** with Sandbox networking on, \\localhost\tiny, \\?\UNC\localhost\tiny, \\COMPUTERNAME\tiny and \\127.0.0.1\tiny each finished with 1 folder unread and gave offered=false. This is the exe-level UNC case the build said it could not make.
- **SUBST under SYSTEM:** a SUBST letter made by SYSTEM opens through GLOBAL??. This confirms the claim in the RescanAsAdministratorProbeTests comment that the code review left unchecked.

**Covered only by unit tests in the suite:**
- the throwing readers (7);
- the CDRom, Ram and other drive types (5);
- the argument quoting for A:\ to Z:\ and a:\ to z:\ (9);
- the declined prompt, error 1223 (10);
- the other refusals and a missing program path (11).

**Criterion 14 was only read, not run.** StartScan:273 calls HideRescanOffer before every scan, and that collapses the button, enables it again and clears its line. This is the design's own declared check. Nothing drove a second scan in the same window.

**Owed to this stage, and not settled:**
- **O-001 (letter shadowing in the elevated session):** cannot be told. It needs a look inside the person's elevated session, and nothing here has one.
- **O-002 (real consent elevation behaves like the spike's token pair):** cannot be told. A real consent prompt cannot be driven. Both are folded into the person-run press check.

I asked for no elevation. Neither named operation would show the app's elevated copy: read-denied-folders turns on SeBackupPrivilege, which the product never does.

**Pattern across this slice:** the guard that only the Click reaches Start has been reopened in every review round. The members still open are on the backlog (SC-087, N-082). That is one rebuild, which changed tests and config only, not a loop in src.

The Sandbox tool left an untracked .taad-scratch/ folder in the worktree. Everything else I made was removed: no app processes left, no SUBST letters, and the deny entry and my scratch folder are gone.

criteria.criterion: 1. Offer on a finished scan of a fixed or removable X:\ (either case) that left ≥1 folder unread, in a copy that is not elevated
criteria.how: Real: D:\ whole-drive report on this PC gave offered=true with 2 unread, from a visible, in-view button. In the Sandbox, a Medium-IL standard user on a global letter with 1 unread gave offered=true. The product probe gives Fixed for C: and D: here. Letter case and \\?\ spellings: RescanAsAdministratorOfferTests in the passing suite.

criteria.criterion: 2. No offer when the scan did not finish: stopped (Cancelled), root unreadable, or refused
criteria.how: Exe level: the script's root-unreadable step reports the key present and false. Every ScanStatus value is covered by the unit test OnlyAScanThatCompletedOffersIt (suite passed). A stopped ending was not run at exe level.

criteria.criterion: 3. No offer, and the report says so, when the root is not a drive letter: folder (with/without trailing backslash), UNC in \\server and \\?\UNC\ spellings
criteria.how: Exe level on this PC: folder and folder-slash (script), and the SUBST target folder (completed, 1 unread, false). Sandbox, standard user: \\localhost\tiny, \\?\UNC\localhost\tiny, \\COMPUTERNAME\tiny and \\127.0.0.1\tiny each finished with 1 unread and offered=false.

criteria.criterion: 4. No offer, and the report says so, on a finished whole-drive scan that read every folder (unreadable 0)
criteria.how: Sandbox, standard user: global T:\ finished with unreadable=0 and offered=false. In the same run, S:\ with 1 unread offered=true. Also ADriveThatWasReadInFullDoesNotOfferIt in the suite.

criteria.criterion: 5. Probe: a network or mapped letter, or a type neither Fixed nor Removable
criteria.how: Real on this PC: the product's probe returns Network for the mapped Z:, and Offers is then false. E: and F: are removable and not ready, so they give null. CDRom, Ram, NoRootDirectory and Unknown are unit-only (ATypeThatIsNotLocal..., suite passed). This PC has none of those drive types.

criteria.criterion: 6. Probe: a global-namespace letter (system drive) against a session-only SUBST letter
criteria.how: Real on this PC: C: and D: give Fixed, and a SUBST letter R: gives null. Report mode on R:\ finished with 1 unread and offered=false. Sandbox: a SUBST letter made by SYSTEM opens through GLOBAL??, as the test's IsSystem branch assumes.

criteria.criterion: 7. Probe: the drive-type read throws IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException or ArgumentException
criteria.how: Code level only: AReadThatThrowsAnIoAccessOrArgumentExceptionGivesNull passes in the full suite. No real drive was made to throw.

criteria.criterion: 8. No offer when the copy is already running elevated
criteria.how: Real in the Sandbox: as SYSTEM, a global Fixed SUBST letter that finished with 1 unread gave offered=false. A standard user on the identical setup gave offered=true. The token was SYSTEM's, not a UAC-elevated admin token on this PC. Both make Environment.IsPrivilegedProcess true.

criteria.criterion: 9. Press: every root A:\..Z:\ and a:\..z:\, exe path with spaces
criteria.how: Code level: EveryDriveRootReachesTheNewCopyAsItsOneArgumentAndNothingElse (52 rows, CommandLineToArgvW split) passes in the suite. No real elevated launch was made.

criteria.criterion: 10. Press: the person declines the UAC prompt (Win32Exception 1223)
criteria.how: Code level: ADeclinedPromptIsTheDeclinedLineAndWindowsIsCalledOnce passes. The real prompt is part of the person-run check below.

criteria.criterion: 11. Press: Windows refuses for another reason (2, 5, 1155), or there is no program path (null/empty)
criteria.how: Code level: AnyOtherRefusalIsTheRefusedLineWithItsCodeAndNoPath and NoProgramFileIsTheNoProgramLineAndWindowsIsNeverCalled pass in the suite.

criteria.criterion: 12. Report-mode scan of a real whole local Fixed drive (least used, not SUBST) that leaves System Volume Information unread shows the offer
criteria.how: Real on this PC: the script picked D: (230,002,659,328 bytes used, opens through GLOBAL??). It finished with 2 folders unread and offered=true, from a visible, in-view button, with the pickers' line height unchanged. The report holds counts only, so I did not see that System Volume Information is one of the 2.

criteria.criterion: 13. The app starts unelevated with no path, with a path, and in report mode, from an unelevated CreateProcess
criteria.how: Real on this PC: the script's no-path and path-window steps stayed up with no exit, and the folder report runs ended exit 0 well inside 60 s. Every manifest in the published exe says asInvoker. The engine saw no prompt it had not raised.

criteria.criterion: 14. Another scan in the same window after an offered ending, pressed or not
criteria.how: Not run. The design's own check is a code review (material false), and I read the code: StartScan:273 HideRescanOffer collapses the button, re-enables it and clears its line before every scan, and ShowOutcome decides again per ending. No run drove a second scan after an offered ending in one window.

criteria.criterion: Pressing it relaunches the app elevated through the UAC prompt and scans the same root
criteria.how:
On this PC, in an ordinary (unelevated) session:
1. Start artifacts\publish\FsAnalyser.App.exe and press the D: drive button. Wait for the finished ending.
2. 'Rescan as administrator' must be on the pickers' line.
3. Press it. Windows' consent prompt for FsAnalyser.App must appear. Choose No. The line beside the button must read 'The rescan as administrator was not started: the Windows prompt was declined.', and the button stays enabled.
4. Press it again and choose Yes. A second window must open and scan D:\ by itself, and must not show the button at its ending.
5. The first window's line must read 'A copy running as administrator was started; it scans this drive again in its own window.', with the button disabled.
6. Its unread count must be no larger than the first window's, and its volume figures must be D:'s (this also covers O-001 and O-002).

obligations.evidence:
I could not look inside an elevated session of the person's account:
- This shell is unelevated.
- The Sandbox runs as SYSTEM with UAC off, so it has no linked elevated session (the spike measured EnableLUA=0).
- Neither named operation (whoami, read-denied-folders) reads another logon session's DOS-device map.

Measured nearby: unelevated on this PC, C: and D: open through GLOBAL?? and the SUBST R: does not. A shadow would have to be made inside the elevated session itself. Only the person-run press shows the outcome: the elevated window's drive figures must match D:.

A real consent elevation cannot be driven from here: the engine forbids raising prompts, and the Sandbox has UAC off.

Measured on the conservative side: unelevated, report mode on a SUBST letter gives offered=false, and the product's probe gives Network for Z:, which Offers refuses. If a real elevation sees more letters than the spike's pair, the gate only refuses a letter that might have worked. The person-run press check covers the interactive case.

not_reached: The UAC press itself: the consent prompt, Yes and No, a new elevated window scanning the same root, and the declined and started lines in a real window. This is person-run.

Whether the elevated copy actually reads more than the limited scan on this PC's real C: or D:. The spike elevated-rescan-reads-what-acl-allows never met its gate. The Sandbox has UAC off, and this shell is not elevated.
Criterion 8 under a UAC-elevated administrator token on this PC. It was measured only as SYSTEM in the Sandbox.
O-001: a session-local definition shadowing a global letter inside the person's elevated session.
Criterion 14 was not driven: no second scan was run in the same window after an offered ending, pressed or not. Code read only.
Whether System Volume Information is one of D:'s 2 unread folders. The report carries counts, never names.
A stopped (Cancelled) ending was not run at exe level (unit-level only).
A removable drive with media, CDRom, Ram or NoRootDirectory drives: none exist on this PC. Those were unit-level only.
A whole-drive report-mode scan of the mapped Z:. Only the probe was read for Z: (Network, never opened). Scanning the share was not run.
N-074: the EnableLinkedConnections=1 setup, where an elevated token might see the limited token's letters.

screens.screen: Main window: the pickers' line, where 'Rescan as administrator' appears at an offering ending
